_notes: Canonical MCP server config for stromy-plugin. Edit only this file. Run scripts/render-mcp.py to regenerate .mcp.json (Claude Code only — this is a distribution product, not a cross-agent workspace, so no .gemini/.codex/.vscode configs are emitted).
_connection_model: Authenticated HTTP MCPs (interactive OAuth, e.g. asset-broker) are consumed as Cowork workspace connectors — do NOT declare them here; a plugin-declared OAuth MCP can only auth via a localhost loopback that fails in remote sessions. Only no-auth HTTP MCPs (stromy-format, nl-gov-data, au-gov-data) and stdio servers belong in a plugin. See infra-docs/ai/mcp-connection-model.md (enforced by validate-plugin-completeness.py Invariant #13).

nl-gov-data._notes: Dutch government open-data MCP — search/fetch legislation, parliamentary records, Rijksoverheid documents, plus the twelve intel/analysis skills (nl-gov-data, nl-monitor, nl-tensions, nl-accountability, nl-policy-legislative-landscape, nl-parliamentary-positioning, nl-issue-framing, nl-dossier-tracker, nl-eu-transposition, nl-evidence-grounding, nl-horizon-scan, nl-guide). Unauthenticated (catalog auth: null; /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp 404s), which is what makes it plugin-declarable under Invariant #13 — an earlier note here claimed per-user Entra OAuth and was wrong. Composes with stromy-format for rendering.

au-gov-data._notes: Australian government open-data MCP — federal legislation (FRL), ABS statistics, AusTender procurement, AEC political finance + electorates, the AGOR organisations register, official feeds, e-petitions, federal parliament, and the cross-jurisdiction Hansard corpus (~888k interventions over 8 parliaments, refreshed daily from au-parliament-data; NT excluded). Unauthenticated, so plugin-declared — no connector step. Two live caveats taught in au-guide: TheyVoteForYou is unkeyed in production (tvfy_* return a disabled envelope, so no Senate voting evidence) and the corpus loads lazily, so a first Hansard call after idle can take ~a minute — bound the first query by jurisdiction + date window. Composes with stromy-format for rendering.

do-gov-data._notes: Dominican Republic government open-data MCP (ORG-PLAN-199) — procurement (DGCP: 621k processes, 708k contracts), budget execution, both chambers with roll-call votes, consolidated law from 1844, Supreme Court + Constitutional Court caselaw, audits, open-data discovery, regulators, and macro. Unauthenticated, so plugin-declared — no connector step. Skills are Spanish; start at do-guide. Three limits it teaches as limits rather than bugs: nothing publishes a law's in-force status (every law record carries an explicit null), consolidated law serves original texts and never consolidates amendments, and granular social statistics are a declared World Bank/CEPALSTAT substitution because the national statistics office has no API and blocks automated access. Shares au-gov-data's ACA environment (subscription env cap, see infra-docs/hosting/azure-regions.md), so its FQDN moves if it is ever given its own. Composes with stromy-format for rendering.

stromy-format._notes: Hosted format skills (format-pptx, format-pptx-hd, format-docx, format-pdf, format-pdf-hd, format-xlsx, format-mermaid, format-diagram, format-chart, format-video-hd). Fetched at runtime via fs_read — see skills/<name>/SKILL.md stubs.

_connectors_note: This plugin is the org's full-fleet dogfooding surface, so it also depends on FOUR OAuth-gated MCPs that are deliberately NOT declared here — Invariant #13 fails a plugin that declares an auth:"oauth" HTTP server, because a remote sandbox cannot complete the localhost loopback callback. They are added once as workspace/desktop connectors and the plugin ships only their skill stubs, which fs_read against the authorized connector at runtime: asset-broker (https://asset-broker-mcp.redbeach-6781a121.northeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp — asset-editor/asset-feedback/asset-brand-studio/asset-website-studio/asset-guide), org-atlas (https://org-atlas-mcp.gentleground-6f68b100.westeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp — org-guide), stromy-workflows (https://stromy-workflows-mcp.happysand-98ed07c8.northeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp — wf-guide/wf-stakeholder-analysis), media-gen (https://media-gen-mcp.whitetree-762cff59.westeurope.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp — media-image-campaign/media-social-pack/media-video-clip/media-guide). All four are Entra app-role gated: an app-role change only enters the roles claim on a FRESH sign-in, so re-authorize the connector after any grant change or every tool call dead-ends while appearing connected.
_apify_note: The official Apify MCP is NOT declared here. It is an authenticated HTTP MCP (hosted https://mcp.apify.com, OAuth) and per the connection model (infra-docs/ai/mcp-connection-model.md) + validate-plugin-completeness Invariant #13, authenticated HTTP MCPs are consumed as Cowork workspace connectors, never plugin-declared. Recommended connector URL (scoped tool surface, pins the curated actors): https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=actors,docs,runs,storage,apify/rag-web-browser,apify/website-content-crawler — client setup steps in skills/research-apify/references/client-onboarding.md. The research-apify skill drives whatever apify connector the workspace has authorized (the client signs into their own Apify account; spend lands there). The earlier stdio BYOK wiring (APIFY_TOKEN set to a dollar-brace env-ref) was dropped because the desktop app does not expand dollar-brace refs in a plugin connector env, so the token never reached the subprocess — see infra-docs/ai/byok-apify-research.md.
